description:
Hi! I’m Shokhrukh, an engineering enthusiast interested in electronics, robotics, and aerospace. I have hands-on experience with engineering projects and robotics competitions.

I’m looking for motivated teammates who enjoy solving problems and turning ideas into reality.

Skills I’m looking for: Programming, data analysis, space science, AI, and UI/UX design.

Let’s combine our skills and build something amazing for NASA Space Apps Challenge! 🚀
summary:
Solar Explorer is an interactive, browser-based 3D visualization platform that makes NASA’s most exciting missions and datasets accessible to everyone. Built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, it integrates real-time planetary ephemeris data from JPL Horizons, NASA’s SPHEREx infrared all-sky survey, and live orbital elements for satellites and space debris.

The platform features a physically accurate solar system with true-scale orbits, an immersive SPHEREx telescope mode showing infrared sky data, a dedicated Planet X search tool highlighting the ~440 AU search zone, and a space debris tracker visualizing over 8,000 catalogued objects by type and size class using ESA MASTER-8 population models.

Users can explore seven iconic NASA mission stories — from Voyager’s Grand Tour to Parker Solar Probe’s record perihelion — with an AI-powered assistant that answers real-time questions about what users see on screen.

Solar Explorer transforms complex NASA data into an engaging, educational experience for students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Solar Explorer is a real-time, browser-based 3D interactive model of the Solar System that integrates multiple NASA datasets into a single immersive experience. Using WebGL and physically accurate orbital mechanics (JPL Horizons ephemeris), users can navigate the Solar System, explore active NASA missions, track space debris, and investigate the infrared universe through NASA’s SPHEREx telescope — all from any browser without installation.

Key Features & Benefits:

  • SPHEREx Integration: A dedicated telescope mode simulates NASA’s SPHEREx infrared all-sky survey (launched 2025), visualizing the 102-band spectral imaging cone and IR background in 3D. Users can upload VarWISE variable star catalogs (CSV) for cross-epoch comparison.
  • Planet X Hunt: An interactive search tool highlighting the hypothetical Planet X search zone (~440 AU), based on 2026 infrared survey strategies.
  • Space Debris Tracker: A 3D Earth globe displays 8,000+ catalogued objects color-coded by type (payload, rocket body, fragment) and size class, using ESA MASTER-8 population models. Includes conjunction screening with probability of collision (Pc) risk levels.
  • Mission Stories: Seven time-accurate mission recreations — Voyager’s Grand Tour (1977–present), New Horizons at Pluto (2015), Parker Solar Probe perihelion (2024), Juno at Jupiter (2016), Psyche Mars flyby (2026), and SPHEREx all-sky survey (2025–2027).
  • AI Assistant: A built-in Claude-powered conversational assistant answers real-time questions about the objects currently visible on screen.
  • Tumble Period Estimator: Simulated light-curve analysis using a 2-stage generalized Lomb–Scargle algorithm (inspired by VARnet) estimates the rotation period of debris objects.

Tools & Technologies Used:

  • Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript (ES2022), WebGL via Three.js, d3-celestial for star maps
  • Orbital Mechanics: satellite.js (SGP4/SDP4 propagator) for TLE-based satellite tracking
  • Data Sources: JPL Horizons (ephemeris), NASA SPHEREx mission data, ESA DISCOSweb, Space-Track.org TLE catalog, Natural Earth geodata
  • AI: Claude API (Anthropic) for the in-app assistant
  • Hosting: Render.com (public, no login required)

Intended Impact:

Space situational awareness and deep-sky science have traditionally been inaccessible to the general public. Solar Explorer bridges this gap by transforming raw NASA datasets into an engaging, educational platform for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. By placing SPHEREx’s science mission — mapping 450 million galaxies and searching for biosignatures — in the context of the full Solar System, the project helps the public understand why infrared astronomy matters and what NASA is currently doing to answer humanity’s biggest questions.

Creativity & Innovation:

Unlike existing tools (NASA Eyes, Stellarium), Solar Explorer uniquely combines: (1) real-time debris risk assessment, (2) SPHEREx spectral imaging simulation, (3) a Planet X hypothesis explorer, and (4) an AI guide — all in a single dependency-free web application weighing under 2 MB.
